column2: A healthy company makes money (margin), grows, has a good reputation and owes little relative to what it sells. Liquidity —cash to pay— matters as much as profit: many profitable companies go bankrupt because they run out of cash.

0–100, with a base of 50: margin × 150, (reputation − 50) × 0.5, sales growth × 60 and debt relative to sales × −15. It is the same health buyers use when bidding for your company. Below you see how many months of expenses its cash covers.
Underpaid or overworked employees perform worse, leave or protest, and that damages the reputation. A company also depends on the health of its sector and its city.

0–100, with a base of 55: wages (±12), workload (−8 at full capacity, −6 with little work), reputation, recent losses (up to −10), health of its sector and demand in the province. Below 30 there is unrest: reputation drops 0.5 every month.
A government can borrow without trouble as long as its economy grows faster than the cost of its debt. With a lot of debt and high rates, more and more taxes go to interest.

0–100, with a base of 60: public debt (−35 to +15), cost of debt against growth plus inflation, treasury, reserves, high inflation, IMF program, war and recession. Below 35 public employees' raises are frozen; below 15 there are job cuts.
Banks, companies and households are connected by loans, sales and jobs: if one link falls, it can drag down the rest. That is why regulators watch the big banks and require more capital.

0–100 (higher is worse), with a base of 20: weak banks, active crisis (+25), high public debt, sectors below 35, households in trouble, an economy concentrated in one sector, neighbors in crisis or recession and reserves that cushion. When a banking crisis breaks out, the neighbors' banks take a hit proportional to the size of that economy.

Everything is connected: a crisis starts in one place and spreads.
  • 🩺 Gauges: in More → 🩺 Health of the economy every company, bank, government and organization has a gauge from 0 to 100 with what pushes it up and what pulls it down. Tap it to see its causes.
  • 💵 Companies: financial health (margin, reputation, growth, debt) and social health (wages, workload, losses, sector and province), and how many months of expenses their cash covers.
  • 🏦 Banks: what moves their health this year and the chance of a banking crisis.
  • 💰 Government: fiscal health (debt, rates, reserves) and social health (approval, stability, happiness, consumption).
  • 🧨 Risk: each country's systemic risk, its contagion chain and the neighbors in crisis. The 🩺 map mode paints it across the whole world.
  • 👨‍👩‍👧 People: your family, your friends and you work in a sector: if it falls, there are cuts and layoffs; if it does well, raises. You can help someone looking for a job with money.
